== Synopsis ==

Once upon a time, there were four little Rabbits, and their names were Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton-tail, and Peter. These four siblings possessed distinctly different natures. The first three—Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail—were good little bunnies, obedient and well-behaved. Their brother Peter, by contrast, was very naughty, and this wayward quality would define his story.

The virtue of Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail manifested itself in their industrious pursuits. One day, these three good rabbits went down the lane to gather blackberries, a wholesome and proper task befitting obedient young rabbits. They undertook this endeavor with the propriety expected of well-behaved siblings.

Peter, being very naughty, refused to follow his siblings' virtuous example. Rather than join Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail in their wholesome task, he ran straight away, choosing instead to pursue his own willful and independent course. In this choice, the naughty rabbit demonstrated the wayward nature that distinguished him from his good siblings.

Presently, as Peter ventured on his own path, he sneezed—'Kertyschoo!'—a small sound marking his solitary journey. Thus begins the tale of this naughty little rabbit, a story set against the contrast of his three obedient siblings and their divergent ways.
